    the boat/minecart branches (it emitted/merged the key before
    but never read it on summon — measured zero). The age step
    gained the `AgeLocked` gate AND the real bug behind it: the
    `else e.Age--` arm ticked a locked baby's age DOWN (−400 →
    −511 in one run) — vanilla's else is `else if (age > 0)`,
    now matched.

    {PortalCooldown:400} counts down through a sprint; a /data
    merge value counts down and clamps at exactly 0;
    chest_minecart (non-Living) decrements identically; a pig
    {Age:-400,AgeLocked:1b} stays −400 over sprint-100 while an
    unlocked sibling climbs to ~−293; ForcedAge:700 never moves.
    Harness fix that mattered: vanilla's /tick sprint is ASYNC —
    commands queued behind it interleave mid-sprint (a first
    data get raced ahead and read the pre-sprint value), so the
    test now waits for the `commands.tick.sprint.report` chat
    before reading counters. Reads use `lastNumberSigned` —
    `lastNumber` silently strips the minus (Age:-400 read 400).

## Slice — shared runtime ownership and public extension lifecycle (2026-10-25)

- **Measured:** code review and Go 1.27.3 race reproduction found per-listener runtime
  ownership, blocking outbound admission without a byte budget, play initialization racing
  wall ticks, live save snapshots outside the owner, internal-only plugin APIs
  and no extension teardown. Bytecode-independent work here uses existing
  wire behavior, race reports and in-process/scripted-client contracts.
- **Implemented:** one idempotent runtime with independent listener attachment
  and terminal joined shutdown; admission gates and joins cover Java, RCON and
  Query. A serial simulation owner covers join/play/leave, commands, ticks,
  frontend actions, queued plugin enforcement and save snapshots. Tick-driver
  exclusion plus complete-tick yields retain step/sprint stop/freeze ingress;
  shutdown interrupts huge tick counts. Save snapshots and disk I/O currently
  run synchronously under ownership and can pause gameplay.
  Public `server`, `api/frontend`, `api/plugin` and `api/event` packages expose

## Slice — finite canonical block views and typed edits (2026-10-25)

- **Measured:** this extension contract has no vanilla API counterpart. Existing
  command-style block mutation semantics were traced at 65119d2 and exercised
  with scripted controls, including powered TNT ending in air and spawning an
  entity. The independent Java consumer reuses official 26.1/26.2 block, item
  and packet reports plus prior public wire/schema facts; its compact manifest
  records tool versions, source/JAR/report checksums and documentation identity.
  No new jar extraction or generated production table is introduced.
- **Implemented:** optional `frontend.Blocks` and public `api/worldview` fixed
  half-open canonical block boxes. One owned boundary flushes prior changes,
  captures a detached x-fastest snapshot and registers the view. Accepted
  `World.SetBlock` writes and Restore deletions invalidate interested cells;
  sparse final reads grouped by shard provide completion barriers. Action ends
  and complete tick yields coalesce final values, independently of Java's
  existing tick-end block/light packet timing. Revisions order observed commits,
  not every world mutation or a whole-world CAS version. Reliability covers
  owner-committed gameplay, commands, typed edits and owned direct writes;
  concurrent raw storage access has no new transaction/snapshot guarantee.
- **Bounds:** 65,536 cells per view, four views per attachment; host defaults
  reserve at most 64 views/1,048,576 cells, 64 MiB queued/reserved payload bytes
  and 4,096 queued/reserved messages. Local queues default to 64 messages/2 MiB.
  Admission precedes payload/baseline/index allocation. Closing or overflowing a
  view releases queued values promptly; cell/view quota remains until owned
  interest removal. Retired handles do not enqueue another cleanup. Other views,
  avatars and attachments continue. Queue budgets exclude checked-out values,
  capture temporaries, backing capacity, adapter copies, GC and total heap.
- **Editing:** explicit dimension, int32 position, complete canonical target and
  copied optional expected-state comparison. Ordered policy can modify only the
  target; veto/cancel/panic/unknown state rejects before writes. Context, bounds,
  catalog and CAS conditions are rechecked after hooks. The existing write
  pipeline retains onPlace/shape, neighbor, container/entity, fluid/redstone and
  lighting side effects. Only the typed privileged entry is hooked: no player
  dig/place simulation, NBT editing, global physics interception or rollback.
  Legacy block observations remain unchanged; typed `TopicBlockEdited` is an
  additive lossy observation, separate from the reliable stream.
- **Receipts:** lifecycle-bound `plugin.BlockEditor` submits callback-safe work
  to the existing 256-action pending queue. Acceptance is not application; one
  buffered outcome then closes, including queued cancel/unload/shutdown/discard.
  Immediate rejection returns no receipt. Running work checks cancellation before
  writing and owns its real result, so late cancellation cannot rewrite success.
  `After` describes immediate synchronous effects; later queued edits or scheduled
  ticks may supersede it before a coalesced delta. No receipt/revision match is
  promised, and callbacks must not wait on the owner for completion.
- **Pinned:** bounded interest union/overlap/Restore and sparse read barriers;
  owner-atomic two-cell snapshots, scheduled lamp updates and command fills;
  detached data, no-op/revert suppression, local/global quota preflight and
  release, cancellation, stale cleanup and overflow isolation. Final storage/
  mailbox/discard race passes in 1.584s, attachment/journal race in 1.568s and
  final retired-Close/quota race in 1.554s. Typed edit/policy/receipt races pass
  API in 1.010s/server in 1.792s, including CAS, exact side effects/persistence,
  active-hook cancellation and Stop during running work. The separate public
  consumer independently materializes a 48-cell Nether volume and real 775/776
  single/section/chunk updates, exercising typed/plugin edits, Java fill/place/
  dig, canonical properties/shifted IDs, rejection/CAS, capture races, overflow,
  detachment and strict old-viewer retirement while 776 receives exact cinnabar.
  It passes normally in 2.334s and under race in 22.524s.
- **Validation:** the full current-source default suite passes, including server
  tests (276.338s), world (0.541s), public/external consumers (10.582s) and the
  full blackbox package (103.989s). Final build, vet and complete public API/
  alias/example races pass. Selected live-vanilla neighbor-fold and redstone
  regressions pass in 74.072s, preserving the existing write pipeline's shape,

  committed source archive with a full build, external public consumers and
  focused world/journal/mailbox/lifecycle/edit tests. No ignored source or
  generated production-table changes are required.
- **Remaining:** these are finite block states only, without neutral lighting,

## Slice — bounded initial Java join preparation (2026-10-25)

- **Measured:** source class is existing Go ownership/cache preparation plus
  scripted public TCP observations, reusing the official report/wire facts
  already pinned for both Java profiles. No new jar extraction, generated table
  or external dependency is introduced. The unchanged TCP harness is SHA-256
  `b529308fcde7e4fbbc912c1134f1cfec366a2c446850a6565c76318f812b5272`;
  its baseline is a clean archive of
  `b4e3e692e0ed3d492a60bf67deded1dbad4e6b3a` with only that file added.
  Sequential five-run baseline/optimized samples use Linux/amd64 Go 1.27.3,
  AMD EPYC 9V74, `GOMAXPROCS=5`, the same radius-2 flat world, ready 775/776
  observers, a distant untouched spawn and new 776 cold/warm joiners. Observer
  tokens have one outstanding request with 20 ms pacing. The initial 775
  mutation/fence sample is separately labeled and excluded from token quantiles.
  Raw phase/readiness/probe start/end timestamps are retained; p50/p95 use
  nearest rank on pooled token-only samples across the five runs.
- **Implemented:** one lazy runtime scheduler, independent of frozen ticks,
  reserves at most 32 building/queued/running jobs before coordinate allocation.
  Radius is bounded at the admitted client maximum 32; coordinate capacities
  total at most 9,530 entries/152,480 bytes per plan on a 64-bit host, plus a
  temporary 5,041-byte deduplication grid. Allocation overhead and total heap
  are separate. Jobs rotate after one complete cold facts column or whole light
  initialization/flood; warm scans yield after at most 64 checks. Work always
  uses the simulation owner. No gameplay action unlocks halfway through a
  mutation, and synchronous plugin callbacks retain their existing boundary.
  Each initialization/flood stays atomic, while valid initialization marks may
  reach existing viewers earlier between units or in different batches.
- **Admission and lifecycle:** preparation resolves only routing scalars from
  the existing spawn/saved-player lookup. The session remains Configuration,
  without a new entity, restored gameplay state or committed presence. Final
  ownership rechecks dimension, coordinates, radius and incarnation before the
  existing atomic Join/opening-batch/attributes/entities/admission transaction.
  Its ordinary cache rechecks can refill facts invalidated during preparation.
  At most three replans follow the initial plan. Saturation, invalid targets,
  exhausted replanning and known cancellation close without invented pre-Join
  packets. Canceled running work retains its slot until its whole unit ends;
  queued work releases immediately, and completed receipts retain no plan arrays.
  Shutdown cancels/joins this scheduler before world workers retire.
- **Responsiveness and tradeoff:** cold full-49-column readiness median grows
  from 865.5 ms (861.9–884.1) to 992.5 ms (980.0–1,052.6), about 14.7%, while
  more observer work completes. The 775 observer has 9 → 175 token samples
  (9 → 172 before readiness), with p50/p95/max 743.4/821.5/821.5 ms becoming
  5.66/16.24/45.68 ms. The 776 observer has 14 → 183 samples (14 → 181 before
  readiness), with 39.79/821.59/821.59 ms becoming 5.33/30.11/45.68 ms.
  This is a responsiveness tradeoff, not a preparation-speed improvement.
  A stalled single outstanding request produces fewer baseline samples; this
  is not a fixed offered-rate capacity test. Timings include transport, commands,
  ticks, decoding and client scheduling. Warm readiness is 61.0 → 60.8 ms with
  overlapping 59.4–72.9/53.4–65.6 ms ranges; warm token maxima are 39–45 ms.
  The separately labeled mutation/fence median is 38.01 → 40.14 ms.
- **Quantum and overhead:** the optimized-only helper/worker benchmark is
  SHA-256 `950293380e9f4bc662e3436dcaffd00d040a8e3b70cf7b36a3835b493c94b9c1`.
  Three 100 ms samples use the existing mixed-canopy, eight-shard radius-2
  fixture without observers, sockets, ticks or pending deferred actions.
  Its 49 facts/121 light units plus completion take 171 owner turns and a
  total median 854.6 ms (828.4–873.2). Helper work timing excludes acquisition
  and boundary flushes: observed maxima are 4.628 ms facts/16.622 ms light.
  Complete uncontended turn wall maxima, including acquisition and empty
  deferred-action/stream-flush boundaries, are 4.630/16.627 ms. Neither is a
  contended owner-hold or tick bound. Warm actual reservation/submission/worker
  completion takes 45.54 µs (44.58–47.93), 288 bytes/two allocations. Separate
  radius-2 plan construction takes 6.237 µs and 3,160 bytes/six allocations;
  radius 32 takes 0.771 ms and 161,112 bytes/six allocations. These are added
  components rather than total warm-join overhead. ARCHITECTURE.md records the
  full fixture, sample counts, limits and reproduction commands.
- **Pinned:** ten deterministic preparation tests pass normally in 0.670 s and
  under race in 9.168 s. They prove real public avatar Move and its committed
  stream update, plus a worldview edit, complete while preparation is unfinished;
  final chunks preserve canonical state. Coverage includes frozen progress,
  whole-unit/64-skip bounds, warm overlap, global reservation/queue retention,
  canceled-running retention, stale receipt isolation, host close, saved/spawn
  target revalidation, bounded retry exhaustion and scheduler shutdown.
  The unchanged TCP probe passes all five baseline runs in 9.826 s and all
  five final optimized runs in 10.654 s, independently decoding complete windows,

  A separate overlapping-viewer pin folds valid initialization/edit updates,

  matching its existing factual manifest; intermediate mark batching is not an

  Actual-vanilla opening-batch, exact initial-chunk and torch-light checks all
  execute without skips and pass in 39.540 s total, using Temurin JDK 25.0.5+8
  and official 26.2 jar SHA-256
  `cdacdfb25898de5e4b4b0e5ddcc2722f77067e46605709c2d886c000ebb63ec5`.
- **Integration regressions:** the initial complete sweep and three isolated
  retries exposed a real first-hit XP failure. Configuring sessions had accrued

- **Validation:** final production sources pass the complete core/public package

- **Remaining:** live movement/teleport windows, save I/O and other long owner

## Slice — cooperative live Java window preparation (2026-10-26)

- **Measured:** source classes are existing Go ownership/cache behavior and
  independent public TCP observations using Go 1.27.3 and Temurin JDK

  and batch-before-forget sequence, without claiming that ordering matches
  vanilla. No new bytecode extraction, generated table or external dependency
  is introduced.
- **Implemented:** already admitted Java movement, teleport, respawn and
  dimension-change paths stage live preparation on the existing scheduler,
  sharing its 32 reserved/building/queued/running jobs with initial joins.
  Pose, hooks and control packets retain whole owned transactions. Fresh
  coordinates and the existing skylight halo stay detached until preparation
  completes; tick/acknowledgement pumps pause the old pending queue without
  consuming batch credit. Each session retains one job and latest scalar
  destination. Generations reject stale A-to-B-to-A, radius, reset, dimension
  and incarnation work; retargeting retains its reservation and drops old
  arrays before replacement. Identical published targets use pump/prune
  directly, including under scheduler saturation. Overflow closes only the
  requesting recipient, without a cold synchronous fallback.
- **Ownership and lifecycle:** ordinary turns complete one cold facts column
  or whole light initialization/flood, or at most 64 warm checks. A final scan
  can visit the bounded plan, refill one invalidated facts column and yield

  existing atomic append/pump/prune sequence. Live terminal reservations retire
  before deferred actions, fixing a successor-window admission gap exposed
  during review. Reset can reuse the same reservation even when marked running;
  retirement cancels it, running work retains quota until its whole unit ends,
  and shutdown joins the shared scheduler before world workers retire. Initial
  join ordering, detached encoder reservations and admitted outbound FIFO
  futures retain their existing contracts.

## Slice — detached public compact world saves (2026-10-26)

- **Measured:** source classes are the existing independently written
  canonical-v2 JSON format, public Go API/artifact observations and fresh
  official 26.1/775 plus 26.2/776 command-wire observations. Go 1.27.3 and
  Temurin JDK 25.0.5+8 probes pin successful `save-all` and `save-all flush`:
  Saving precedes Success for the caller, while only Success echoes to the
  second operator. The compact manifest records probe/log/oracle SHA-256.
  These vanilla commands exercise native persistence and do not establish
  compact Go save or restart semantics. No new bytecode extraction, generated
  table or external dependency is introduced.
- **Implemented:** public `SaveWorld` in compact `WorldPath` mode reserves
  one unfinished job before capturing every dimension's override map, immutable
  catalog and destination path under simulation ownership. Canonical conversion,
  sorting, JSON serialization and file writes use only detached values outside
  ownership. The caller waits outside ownership for its own actual write result.
  Busy public callers retain no new snapshot, wait outside ownership, then
  recheck shutdown and capture their own state when admitted. This limits jobs,
  not bytes: capture/storage remain O(total overrides), with serialization
  temporaries additional. Capture itself can still pause gameplay.
- **Ordering and lifecycle:** compact `/save-all` uses the same writer fence,
  waits for prior submitted work, then captures and waits for its own save
  under ownership. The worker never needs the owner, preventing that wait from
  inverting ownership. A final admission check rejects an owned waiter if
  shutdown starts before its capture. Shutdown drains accepted detached work
  before world workers retire and rejects unadmitted requests, without starting
  a new save. Native `WorldDir`, `SaveServerData` and player/block-entity paths
  retain their existing owner-blocking behavior. Main still calls `SaveWorld`
  then `SaveServerData` separately; this adds no cross-store atomicity.

  `eb31a9b9f5037b352f78c7f1e6d6786d7b1c629c028d21a98938886a5a1b7d0a`.

## Slice — normal world type: generated overworld in the server (2026-10-29)

- **Measured:** wire observation of a 26.2 server on `level-type=minecraft:normal`
  (seed 12345, the stage data pack stripping features, structures off):
  Set Default Spawn Position, every streamed Chunk Data packet's
  heightmaps, section counts, block and biome palettes and light.
  Bytecode inspection of `PalettedContainer.Strategy` (biomes go global
  past 3 bits, block states past 8), `Heightmap.Types` predicates and
  `MinecraftServer.setInitialSpawn` / `PlayerSpawnFinder.getSpawnPosInChunk`
  (climate `findSpawnPosition` chunk, 11x11 chunk spiral). Per-state
  light emission comes from the `tools/genblockprops` jar oracle table.
- **Implemented:** `-level-type normal` (and level.dat's generator) swaps
  the overworld for a provided world fed by `terrainSource`: terrain is
  generated in parallel and ahead (7x7 around a request), decoration
  runs one chunk at a time once a chunk's 3x3 has terrain, and a chunk
  is handed out once its 3x3 is decorated; protos are pruned once
  nothing can read them. The world keeps a base-chunk cache (saved
  chunks install straight from region files; all generated chunks save
  with per-cell biome palettes). Packet and save heightmaps use the exact
  per-type predicates; section biome palettes follow vanilla's
  strategy; light emission is the jar's per-state value (the curated
  name table had 609 wrong states). Block light moved to per-section
  arrays; a generated chunk's emitters (and its lit neighbours') are
  spread when it is first encoded, and its neighbours are lit before
  it is sent so light crossing its borders is in place.
- **Pinned:** `TestNormalWorldChunkParity` joins both servers and
  compares the world spawn and every chunk both windows streamed (42-49
  chunks): block states, heightmaps, section counts and biome cells
  match exactly, as does block light; `TestNormalWorldSaveReload` saves
  and reloads a generated world (generator, spawn, edits, installed
  chunks, deterministic regeneration).
- **Remaining:** sky light differs in a few enclosed cave pockets where
  vanilla holds 1-10 and mc-go 0 (8-9 of ~1100 sections; logged by the
  test); fluid post-processing; generation speed (~70 ms of terrain per
  chunk on one core, so a fresh join waits ~15 s on a busy 4-core box
  against vanilla's spawn pre-generation); features beyond ores,
  structures, nether/end generation.

## Slice — nether and end generation, generated-chunk light parity (2026-10-29)

## Slice — generation post-processing: marked fluids tick (2026-10-29)

- **Measured:** bytecode inspection of `LevelChunk.postProcessGeneration`:
  per section, every marked position (aquifer, carver and feature marks,
  `ProtoChunk.markPosForPostProcessing` order) with a non-empty fluid
  gets `FluidState.tick` immediately, a `LiquidBlock` gets its block
  tick (the bubble-column rebuild), anything else
  `Block.updateFromNeighbourShapes` with flags 276; it runs as the chunk
  becomes ticking. Wire observation: a generated window left ticking
  for a minute on the real server (random ticks off) against mc-go.
- **Implemented:** generated base chunks carry their marked fluid cells
  (`ProtoChunk.PostProcessFluids`); the bubble-column half runs on the
  decorated proto (`PostProcessBubbleColumns`); the server ticks each
  marked fluid once (`postProcessStep`, after the scheduled ticks) when
  the chunk's eight neighbours exist, and the flows run on through the
  scheduled fluid ticks.
- **Pinned:** `TestNormalWorldSettledParity` joins, lets the window tick
  for a minute with `random_tick_speed 0`, rejoins and compares every
  overlapping chunk strictly (no fluid exemption) - blocks, heightmaps,
  counts, biomes, light and masks.
- **Remaining:** the shape-update half for non-fluid marks (vanilla's
  `updateFromNeighbourShapes`), post-processing lists in saved chunks,
  ticking-level timing (mc-go runs the pass once neighbours exist).

Focused runs used -vet=off after an unrelated transient furnace-output symbol error from concurrent edits; parent must run full vet on the stable integrated tree.

## Slice — packet framing across read deadlines (2026-10-29)

- **Measured:** independent scripted protocol reads against mc-go's Reader,
  using Go 1.27.3's network-deadline error contract. Before the fix, a deadline
  after the first byte of a frame-length prefix made the retry return an
  apparently valid packet with an empty payload. A retry after compression
  negotiation returned unexpected EOF. These are deterministic local framing
  failures; no vanilla implementation or source is used.
- **Implemented:** Reader retains partial outer-length and bounded frame-body
  progress when an underlying read returns a network timeout. Clearing the
  deadline and retrying resumes the same frame. Terminal I/O errors, malformed
  lengths and completed frames discard partial state as before. Compression
  negotiation and existing outer/inflated length limits remain intact.
- **Pinned:** `TestReaderResumesEveryFrameDeadline` covers all 304 plain and
  319 compressed frame byte boundaries, then verifies the following packet.
  Additional tests cover a three-byte length, compression negotiation, real
  fragmented net.Pipe deadline reads and existing EOF/malformed/limit errors.
  The complete protocol package passes (0.182 s before the additional pipe
  cases); the final complete package with the race detector passes (1.988 s).
  `collectJoin` now reports a received disconnect's reason instead of losing
  it behind a later EOF. The original portal baseline separately passes
  (136.20 s) at calmer load, with all 49 destination chunks and their light
  matching exactly. The fixed-Reader `TestPortalDestinationParity` passes (156.60 s),
  again with all 49 chunks/light/arrivals matching, and
  `TestBadHandshakeParity` (18.03 s) and `TestOversizeFrameParity` (16.00 s)
  pass with their original assertions.
- **Remaining:** neither the original portal EOF nor the potion drain EOF is
  attributed to this retry bug without a captured interrupted frame. Cold
  generation latency and complete connection-liveness parity remain separate.

## Slice — heartbeat timeout after actual delivery (2026-10-29)

- **Measured:** independent Go 1.27.3 scripted net.Pipe clients reading an
  outbound FIFO held by an unfinished server-generated chunk. Before the
  fix a healthy reader is marked timed out after 0.15 s although no heartbeat
  can reach the wire. These clients use no read deadlines, separating this
  server availability bug from the packet-framing retry bug. No vanilla
  counterpart exists for mc-go's detached chunk-future fixture.
- **Implemented:** the response window starts only after the first unanswered
  heartbeat is written. Later heartbeat writes retain that first deadline;
  any incoming client packet resets it. Successful write completion checks
  for responses that arrived before or during completion, preventing an
  already answered request from being marked pending again. Configuration
  and watchdog documentation now describe this response-window contract.
- **Pinned:** `TestKeepAliveWaitsForChunkDelivery` covers queued output,
  heartbeat echoes, other packet responses, finite silent-client expiry and
  future cancellation. `TestKeepAliveEchoBeforeWriteCompletion` holds the
  completed network write until its echo has been processed, then places
  unfinished output behind it. The targeted KeepAlive/Outbound/ChunkFuture/
  ChunkPool/shutdown suite passes (3.221 s). The focused race suite, including
  ordinary TCP keepalive ack/expiry and session-close/shutdown races, passes
  (20.802 s).
- **Remaining:** full vanilla heartbeat cadence, challenge semantics and
  latency calculation remain separate from this delivery-availability pin.
  This independently proven bug is not attributed as the cause of the
  earlier portal or potion EOF without a captured connection failure.

Creative plus level2 is required; wrong entity ids/types are silent. Edits replace command, reset success count, change tracking, clear disabled output and acknowledge nonempty commands with enabled/disabled feedback. Disabled execution still accepts edits but skips synced metadata updates. Metadata13 is the command string and14 the output component.

The minecart metadata callbacks differ from blocks: loading a nonempty command changes metadata13 and calls setCommand again, resetting the loaded success count. Fresh loading with disabled tracking discards hidden output/time fields instead of resurrecting them.
